title: How do we find every angle in a figure?
description: A figure of many lines hides many angles. Each place where lines meet is checked, the rays that start there are paired up, and each angle is named with three letters. Each angle is then guessed, measured and recorded in a table.
teaching_notes: One idea: look at each place where lines meet, pair up the rays that start there, and name every pair with the vertex letter in the middle. Watch for students who stop after the first few angles, since the book says to try more.

video_script.why: The child lists the angles of a figure one meeting place at a time, names them with the vertex in the middle, and then compares a guess with a measured size, as in the guessing game.
video_script.substitution: The figure of the book with the letters A, P, R, B, C, D, L and S.
video_script.anchor: the figure of the book, made of lines, with the letters A, P, R along the top, B at the right, C at the left, and D, L, S along the bottom
video_script.payoff_line: Here are ten angles in the figure

final_answer.spoken: there are more angles to find

maths_rules: an angle is made by two rays that start at one point, the vertex
two rays that start at one vertex make one angle, so 3 rays make 3 angles and 4 rays make 6 angles
an angle is named with three letters, and the letter of the vertex goes in the middle
the book lists CAP, ACD, APL, DLP, RPL, SLP, PRS, LSR, BRS, CLP and says try more
the gap between a guess and a measure is the smaller number taken from the bigger number
video_script.design: The figure stays on the board. The meeting places light up, the rays at each place are paired, and the angle names are held back until the answer line. The video ends by saying that more angles are still to find.
open_questions: The figure is not in the extracted text, so the measures are not given. The video teaches how to list, guess and measure, and does not state any size.
The book lists ten angles and says Try more, so the list is not complete. The video says that more angles are still to find.

narration: <bookmark mark='rays'/>Step two, stand at one place and list the rays that start there.
<bookmark mark='pair'/>Any two of these rays make an angle.
<bookmark mark='three'/>With three rays at a place, there are three pairs, so there are three angles.
